$comment: Derived from env-007: the same envelope and the same committed signature (kat-envelope-002-ed25519, signed by kat-keypair-001), with `version` changed from `aitp/0.3` to `aitp/9.9` after signing. `aitp/9.9` is chosen because no release will assign it. The previous revision `aitp/0.2` is covered separately by env-011, whose signature is valid for its own bytes. The signature verifies over the original envelope and not over this one (both checked by scripts/verify-known-answer.mjs and scripts/recompute-known-answer-independent.py), so a verifier that checked the signature first would report INVALID_SIGNATURE; the RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4 check order puts `version` first. The envelope schema's `version` const also rejects the value, so schema validation alone would give the wrong code too. Reusing env-007's message_id is safe: each fixture runs against fresh verifier state.
description: Envelope whose `version` was changed after signing to a value the receiver does not implement. RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4 check order: `version` is checked first and an unknown value is rejected with UNKNOWN_VERSION (§7) before the member set or the signature is examined. Expected: UNKNOWN_VERSION, not INVALID_SIGNATURE or UNKNOWN_FIELD.

expected.rationale: `version` is `aitp/9.9`, which the receiver does not implement. The RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4 check order rejects an unknown `version` with UNKNOWN_VERSION before checking the member set (UNKNOWN_FIELD) or the signature (INVALID_SIGNATURE), even though the signature also fails.
